rules.description: A tip that has been in another liquid touches the liquid of a stock (a well that held liquid from the start and that the protocol draws from). Error if the stock is drawn from again and the trace reaches wells it was never meant for; warning otherwise.
A tip that has been in a liquid touches the liquid of a well into which the protocol never transfers that liquid on purpose, before or after. Warning.
A well that holds liquid receives a different liquid, and liquid is later drawn out of it with no mixing of that well in between. Warning.

A run of mixing strokes that cannot mix the well. A mix counts only if the strokes together move about two wells' worth of liquid (the number is in the rulebook), there are at least three of them, and no stroke is the whole well. Warning. Silent on a well of unknown volume, a well holding one liquid (a pre-wet), a stock only drawn from, and a single stroke followed by a draw from the same well (a prime). When the well holds more than the pipette can draw, the strokes are measured against the pipette instead, and a pipette that cannot draw a fifth of the well fires whatever the count.
An aspirate below the pipette's minimum volume is an error: the amount cannot be measured, and the simulator does not notice.

A dispense takes a well past its rim, by the labware definition's shape: error. Past the maker's stated maximum but under the rim, or where no rim is known: warning. Mixing in a well 90% full or more: warning. Declaring that a well starts with more liquid than it holds: note. Waste and trash labware, and reservoirs, tubes, beakers, bottles, troughs or containers only ever poured into, are exempt (a plate never is). When a pause comes between the well's last draw and the crossing, the finding says so.
An aspirate whose tip is above the liquid in a well of known shape draws air: every well filled from it is short. The simulator does not notice.

Labware sits on a temperature module, and liquid is drawn from or put into it before the protocol ever sets the module's temperature: the block is at room temperature until it is set. Warning, once per labware; if a cold setting (10 C or below) comes later, the finding says at which line. A module used first and then set warm is a planned incubation and is left alone, as are thermocyclers, heater-shakers and untouched labware.

At the end of the run a well holds two or more different liquids, the last one added was under 30% of the well, and nothing mixed the well or drew from it afterwards. Note when the well holds a PCR liquid (the plate is vortexed before cycling); otherwise warning when the liquid added last is a sample, note if not. Silent on waste and trash, and on a reservoir channel only ever poured into.

A PCR or qPCR plate has no well with the mix and no sample: note. The plate counts as a PCR plate when a master mix or polymerase and samples end up together in at least four wells. A dilution series of one sample has no well of diluent without sample: note. A reverse transcriptase reaches the reaction wells and no well has the same contents without it: note. Silent when no liquids are declared, and under four reaction wells.

A well receives an enzyme, polymerase or master mix straight from its stock, and water or buffer comes afterwards, when the well held less than 50% of its final water or buffer at the time. Warning. Silent when no liquids are declared, when the liquid arrives inside a mix made in another tube, or when the mix is itself the bulk of the reaction.

A tip that has been in a sample touches the liquid of a well holding a reagent into which the protocol never transfers that liquid on purpose. Warning. Proposed by example: reported as a note until adopted.

findings.title: No blank on a dilution series: 8 wells of bsa
findings.explanation: At line 29 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1): 8 wells at 8 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 1.
findings.fix: Add a well of water alone, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: A used tip carried water (tube A2 in slot 3) into well A1 in slot 1 it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 39 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 1 while it still carried water (tube A2 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 39. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.
